chunks: And as for what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Hajj of the poor (al-sarurah) is valid for him and for whoever performs Hajj on his behalf; it does not contradict the first report because the meaning of his statement 'it is valid for him' is as long as he is poor and has no wealth. When he becomes wealthy, Hajj becomes obligatory upon him, according to what the first report contained. And we said this because it is ambiguous and open to interpretation, while the first report is detailed, and ruling based on the detailed report regarding the ambiguous one is more appropriate.

key_terms.الصَّرُورَةِ: The poor person (one with limited means)

ai.seo_question: Does a poor person need to perform Hajj again after becoming wealthy?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *tarjih* (preference), prioritizing the detailed report (*mufassal*) over the ambiguous one (*mujmal*) to establish that Hajj al-sarurah serves as a preliminary discharge of duty rather than a final fulfillment. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the obligation remains pending until one possesses sufficient surplus wealth, ensuring the ritual is performed with the requisite capacity.
